title: Buying a Home From Out of State: A Practical Guide
description: Buying a home from out of state means relying on virtual tours and good process. Here is how financing, inspections, and closing work when you can't be there.
keyword: buying a home from out of state
body:
Buying a home from out of state means you may make a very large decision after seeing the place mostly on a screen. That can work, but it takes a clear process and a few checks that replace the walk-through you can't do in person.

This guide covers the steps I'd put in order: financing, virtual tours, reading the local market, verifying address-specific details, and closing from a distance.

## Get your financing sorted first

{{img:0}}

Start with a pre-approval, not a pre-qualification. Pre-approval means a lender has actually reviewed your documents. That matters when you are making decisions quickly and can't drive over for a second look.

Rates also shape your budget. Freddie Mac reported the 30-year fixed mortgage rate at 7.28% for the week of 2026-10-01 (Freddie Mac via FRED). Rates change weekly, so treat any number as a snapshot. You can test payments with the [mortgage calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and read the plain-language guides at the [CFPB Owning a Home guides](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/).

A few other basics apply no matter where you live:

- Private mortgage insurance is typically required on conventional loans when the down payment is under 20 percent.
- FHA loans allow a down payment as low as 3.5 percent.
- VA loans typically require no down payment and no monthly mortgage insurance, though a funding fee may apply.

From the day you apply through closing, avoid opening new credit, financing furniture, or changing jobs. Relocation often involves a job change, so talk to your lender early about timing. I can't give lending advice, but a licensed lender can.

## Use virtual tours, and know their limits

Video walk-throughs and live video tours are useful for layout, light, and flow. They are less useful for things a camera can't show: smells, noise, water pressure, or how a street feels at different times of day.

Here are ways to fill the gaps:

- Ask for a live video tour where you can direct the camera, rather than only watching a recorded one.
- Request a second walk-through at a different time of day.
- Read the seller's documents carefully. Tennessee sellers complete the residential property condition disclosure (or an exemption), and the lead-based paint disclosure applies to homes built before 1978.
- Plan for a full home inspection, done by someone who is physically there on your behalf.

Common add-ons to a standard inspection include radon testing, a sewer scope, and a termite inspection. Termite and wood-destroying organism (WDO) inspections are commonly requested by buyers and lenders in Tennessee. If you want background on radon, the [EPA radon information](https://www.epa.gov/radon) page explains it in plain terms.

If you can manage one trip, make it a short one after your offer is accepted, timed around the inspection. Seeing the home in person before the end of your inspection period gives you one more chance to ask questions.

## Read the local market, not national headlines

{{img:1}}

Middle Tennessee is not one market. Numbers vary by town, and what you read about the country as a whole may not describe the street you are considering.

Months of supply is how long it would take to sell every active listing at the current pace of sales. Under 4 months favors sellers, 4 to 6 months is balanced, and over 6 months favors buyers.

Here is a snapshot from Redfin's rolling 3-month data as of 2026-08-31:

- Franklin: 3.6 months of supply, median days on market 49, average sale-to-list ratio 98.3%.
- Spring Hill: 4.1 months of supply, median days on market 62, average sale-to-list ratio 98.8%.
- Nashville: 5.8 months of supply, median days on market 64, average sale-to-list ratio 97.6%.

For the wider Nashville metro, Redfin's 4 weeks ending 2026-09-27 show a median sale price of $461,491 and 5.6 months of supply. These are past figures, not predictions, and a single home can differ a lot from any median.

You can see more on the [market data page for the I-65 corridor](/market-data), and the [Franklin area guide](/areas/franklin) and [Spring Hill area guide](/areas/spring-hill) cover the basics of each place.

One geography note that trips up many people: Spring Hill includes parts of both Williamson and Maury counties, so county services, schools, and taxes can differ by address. Murfreesboro is in Rutherford County and Columbia is in Maury County. Neither is in Williamson County.

## Verify what depends on the exact address

When you can't visit, it is tempting to rely on a summary. Some details, though, only come from official sources for a specific address.

- **Schools:** School assignment depends on the exact address. Confirm it with the district, such as [Williamson County Schools](https://www.wcs.edu), for any home you are serious about.
- **Property taxes:** These also depend on the address. Check with the county. The [Williamson County property search](https://www.williamsoncounty-tn.gov/2099/35739/Property-Data-Search) is a place to start for homes in that county. For Spring Hill, confirm which county the address falls in.
- **City services:** Rules and services vary by city, so check the municipality's website, such as the [City of Spring Hill](https://www.springhilltn.org).

I'd rather you confirm these yourself than take anyone's word for it, including mine.

## Closing from a distance

Most of closing can be handled remotely, but a few points deserve extra attention.

**Costs.** Closing costs typically run 2 to 4 percent of the purchase price, plus earnest money and moving costs.

**The Closing Disclosure.** A lender must send it at least 3 business days before closing. Compare it with your Loan Estimate and ask questions about anything that changed.

**Wire fraud.** It is real. Verify wire instructions by phone using a number you already trust, and never rely on emailed wire instructions. This is especially important when you are far away and doing everything by email.

**Moving.** Request quotes from at least 3 licensed moving companies and book early for month-end dates. Our [moving checklists](/checklists) can help you keep track of tasks on both ends.

**Your old home.** If you are selling where you live now, cancel homeowner's insurance on that home only after closing is confirmed.

You can also look up an agent's license on the Tennessee Real Estate Commission site, which is a good habit for anyone you hire remotely.

## A reasonable next step

Buying from a distance goes more smoothly when someone on the ground is answering questions and coordinating details. If you are planning a move to Middle Tennessee, fill out the [Get Matched form](/buy#form). I schedule a call, and you will be talking with me within the next 48 hours. If you would rather start with a question, you can [contact me directly](/contact).

— Scott Davis, REALTOR® with Hive Nashville

faq.q: Can you buy a house without seeing it in person?
faq.a: Yes, many buyers do. Video tours, seller disclosures, and a full home inspection done by someone on site help fill in what you can't see yourself.

faq.q: What is the difference between pre-approval and pre-qualification?
faq.a: Pre-approval means a lender has reviewed your documents. Pre-qualification is a looser estimate, so pre-approval is generally the stronger step when you are buying from a distance.

faq.q: How much are closing costs when buying a home?
faq.a: Closing costs typically run 2 to 4 percent of the purchase price, plus earnest money and moving costs.

faq.q: How do I avoid wire fraud at closing?
faq.a: Verify wire instructions by phone using a number you already trust. Never rely on wire instructions sent by email.

faq.q: Is Spring Hill in Williamson County?
faq.a: Spring Hill includes parts of both Williamson and Maury counties, so county services, schools, and taxes can differ by address.
